title: DOT Hazardous Materials Training (49 CFR)
releaseBlockers: covers highway carriage only: rail, air and vessel parts (174–176) and packaging parts (179–180) were not researched
PHMSA's site (phmsa.dot.gov) refused automated requests, so its guidance and the Emergency Response Guidebook are not used
description: US DOT hazmat employee training: every idea explained before it is tested, every card quoting the regulation's own words.
notice: This deck covers topics in the hazardous materials training that 49 CFR 172.704 requires employers to give their hazmat employees. It is built from the text of the Hazardous Materials Regulations (49 CFR parts 171 to 180) and Federal Register final rules, which are U.S. Government works. It is independent and is not affiliated with, sponsored, endorsed or approved by the U.S. Department of Transportation or the Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA). Studying it is not hazmat training under 49 CFR 172.704. Only a hazmat employer can train, test and certify its hazmat employees. It is not legal advice. Always check the current regulation.

glossary.HM: hazardous material (as in the HM column of the Hazardous Materials Table)
glossary.NA: North America (as in NA identification numbers)

checks.what: Three independent audits read all 810 cards against 49 CFR as published on govinfo, found word for word by the card checker; every table cell was read in the page layout, and all 49 label, placard and mark figures were compared with the CFR's own images
checks.result: Three wrong cards fixed: a reporting scenario where the small-release exception made a second answer defensible, a placarding card overtaken by the 2026 exemption for empty IBCs, and a combustible-liquid explanation. Two unsupported claims removed (one said alternate names were allowed only for international transport); 5 ambiguous and 8 unclear cards and 27 minor issues fixed.
